contract: A BLOCK-level node sitting inside an INLINE array — {"type":"paragraph","content":[…]} or {"type":"list-item","content":[…]} — carries its text one level deeper than an inline walk looks, so it composes to nothing and the prose vanishes while it sits intact in storage. Measured 2026-09-02 on the live corpus: 75 list items across 4 published papers rendered as an empty bullet. PR #15701 fixed the Elixir engine at its shared inline-run walk; this fixture is the cross-engine lock so the Go TUI reader and the @barkpark/react SDK cannot diverge from it again. THE LAW: before walking a run of inline nodes, replace any node carrying a NON-EMPTY LIST under `content` with that list — ONE level, never recursively. Keyed on `content` rather than a type allowlist because no inline node type in any of the three engines reads `content` (inline nodes carry `value`, `text`, `children` and marks), so the key cannot shadow a legitimate inline node. The unwrap belongs to the RUN walk only (compose_inline_children/1 · InlineRenderer.Inline · renderInlines) — a mark node's own children walk (compose_inline/2 · InlineRenderer.children · renderInlineChildren) is deliberately NOT unwrapped, matching the Elixir original.

cases.name: a paragraph wrapper carries its prose one level deep
a list-item wrapper carries its prose one level deep
a wrapper holding several inline leaves keeps their order
a wrapper beside plain sibling leaves splices in place
a wrapper holding a mark node renders that node normally
a heading wrapper unwraps too — keyed on content, not a type allowlist
an unheard-of block type unwraps too — the key is the field, not the name
a wrapper with EMPTY content keeps today's behaviour (nothing)
a node whose content is a STRING is not a wrapper and is not unwrapped
ONE level only — a wrapper inside a wrapper is not unwrapped twice
CONTROL — a plain text leaf is untouched
CONTROL — an inline mark node with children is untouched
CONTROL — an inline code leaf keeps reading value, not content
